verification_report.summary: The proposition, its proof, and both sharpness assertions are correct under the stated conventions and accepted inputs. The zero-mass reduction is valid; the adjoint Fredholm problem is correctly normalized using the Gauduchon identity, index zero, and the one-dimensional kernels; the W^{2,p}-to-C^1 estimate yields the linear reverse control; and uniform smoothing of bounded-Lipschitz tests yields the square-root upper control after optimization. On the flat torus, the dd^c normalization, positivity, L^1 norm, admissible test function, and integral 1/(8 pi k) all compute as stated. The k-family rules out every upper exponent greater than 1/2, while the t-family rules out every superlinear exponent for the inverse modulus (equivalently every lower-power exponent below one in the displayed lower bound). There are no external-paper citations requiring arXiv or web verification.
